articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumped AWS GovCloud keys on public GitHub like it's their personal diary. When the agency responsible for cybersecurity can't secure their own crown jewels, you know we're living in the best timeline.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: Critical RCE in Gogs Git service sits unfixed since March while maintainers ghost the researcher. Exploit module already in the wild because apparently responsible disclosure is a one-way street.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: Palo Alto's GlobalProtect auth bypass (CVE-2026-0257) getting hammered in the wild. Nothing says 'enterprise security' like your VPN gateway becoming a welcome mat for attackers.

articles.title: New infostealer reaches enterprise devices through FortiClient EMS vulnerability
articles.summary: Microsoft throws tantrum after researcher dumps zero-days without permission. Maybe if Redmond actually responded to vulnerability reports instead of playing dead, this wouldn't happen.

articles.title: New infosec products of the month: May 2026
articles.summary: Researcher drops 6 Windows zero-days after Microsoft ignores them, now 3 are being exploited. Classic tale of 'responsible disclosure' meeting corporate indifference — guess who wins?

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification laws create surveillance dystopia for everyone while pretending to protect kids. Because nothing says 'child safety' like forcing adults to upload government IDs to access memes.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: License plate readers now used for school residency checks and noise complaints because mission creep never met a surveillance tool it didn't love. Your commute is now evidence for everything.

articles.title: Microsoft Calls the Zero-Day Dumps Irresponsible. The Researcher Says Microsoft Started It.
articles.summary: Attackers hijack FortiClient EMS vulnerability to push enterprise infostealer disguised as legit updates. When your security vendor becomes the attack vector, that's peak 2026 energy.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: 23andMe lawsuit reveals they downplayed massive DNA breach while allegedly paying ransom. Your genetic secrets: stolen, sold, and covered up — but hey, at least you know you're 2% Viking.

articles.title: Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw to Deploy Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Critical RCE in Gogs Git service scores 9.4 CVSS, lets any authenticated user own the server. Self-hosted Git repos becoming self-owned faster than you can say 'git push origin pwned'.
